messages:
cassie: heads up — small-pod eviction spike in ap-southeast1c since ~12:10 UTC. lots of tiny jobs piling Pending. looks like slot-mosaic fragmentation + conntrack flaps 

matt: saw it too, ~30-50 tiny pods queued. preemptions kicked in and we saw attach/detach latency climb. any obvious root cause yet? :eyes:

jordan: can you paste one of the pending pod describes and any scheduler events?

cassie: paste below — one example (redacted names):
```
Name:         mini-serve-xyz
Namespace:    workloads
Node-Selectors:  gpu=rtx
Tolerations:  gpu=reserved:NoSchedule
Events:
  12m   Warning   FailedScheduling   3/4 nodes had taints that the pod didn't tolerate
  12m   Normal    SchedulingAttempt  Attempted to bind to node/gpu-03 but reservation mismatch
  11m   Normal    Preemption        Preempted 2 tiny-pods to make room
```

cassie: also seeing repeated connect errors from node-proxy to netns on a couple of nodes — suspecting sporadic conntrack exhaustion causing attach/detach retries. warmpool handoffs are timing out so scheduler marks nodes unavailable and fragmentation spikes.

priya: we rolled a small label/taint change yesterday to isolate a new reserved pool — maybe label-syncer lagged during rollout? can we check label-syncer restart counts and the controller logs?

matt: grabbing label-syncer logs and pod-restart history now. if syncer is lagging that could explain why pods think nodes are tainted even though they should tolerate.

jordan: short term mitigation: relax the strict-affinity gate for tiny pods so warmpool can accept them despite mismatch. would reduce churn but increases cross-tenant packing risk.

lee: agree with jordan for short term. run a 30m policy relax for tiny-pod class and monitor cost. also we should throttle preemptions; they seem to cascade when attach/detach timeouts happen.

matt: cost note — relaxing will let more tiny pods land on reserved GPUs and increase per-minute spend (ballpark +8–12% in ap-southeast1 on current mix). worth it to stop the evict loop?

cassie: prefer reliability > small cost bump for next few hours if it stops the eviction spiral. I'll patch scheduler policy to allow tiny-pod soft-affinity override for 1h as canary.

ops-bot: autoscaler: scaled up nodepool-ap-se1 by 2 nodes at 12:34 UTC (reason: pending pods threshold breached) :white_check_mark:

matt: logged: label-syncer restarted 3x in last 20m — OOMKilled on one controller instance. pushing a restart with increased memory cap now.

priya: filing an incident checklist item: investigate why label-syncer OOMs during rollout. probable cause: cache blow-up from namespace storm + expensive label reconcile.

jordan: after cassie patches the scheduler, can we run a test that simulates attach/detach delay to ensure preemption doesn't thrash? I have a small script.

cassie: running the patch now (applying canary soft-affinity override). will post results in ~5m.

cassie: update 12:44 UTC — canary applied, pending queue dropped from ~48 -> 6, preemptions slowed. still seeing 2 nodes with netns errors, placing a cordon on them to stop further churn.

lee: cordon + fix is good. after we stabilize, we should run a controlled drain on the two flaky nodes and trigger conntrack cleanup. add a playbook step to scrub conntrack and reboot kernel modules if necessary.

matt: label-syncer memory bump rolled out, no restarts in the last 8m. logs look cleaner.

priya: action items: 1) postmortem on label-syncer OOM + reconcile performance, 2) improve warmpool handoff timeouts/backsoff, 3) add alert when tiny-pod queue > 20 for >5m.

jordan: i'll run the attach/detach stress script in a canary namespace for 15m to validate preempt throttle.

cassie: thanks — current plan: keep soft-affinity override for 1h, cordon flaky nodes, run drain+conntrack scrub, monitor costs. i'll update ops-runbook with the temporary relaxation and rollback steps. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: deploy-bot: scheduler-config canary applied by cassie at 12:45 UTC — monitor link: https://grafana/redwood/scheduler-canary

cassie: final 12:55 UTC — queue back to normal levels, preemptions normalized. leaving canary on for another 20m then will roll back if stable. closing loop in incident tracker.

matt: nice work team. we'll follow up with a cost/regression eval tomorrow.

priya: assigning postmortem owner: matt.

jordan: two follow-ups: add label-syncer horizontal autoscaling based on queue size, and consider making warmpool handoff fallback smarter (retry with exponential backoff instead of instant preempt).

cassie: noted. I'll add those to the infra backlog.

lee: bravo. :clap:
